metadata.title: After Q3 2026, What Coinbase’s Revenue Mix Says About Its Valuation

content.text:
By Exec Edge Editorial Staff
In the third quarter of 2026, Coinbase Global, Inc. (NASDAQ: COIN) reported total revenue of $1.2 billion, net income of $719 million, adjusted EBITDA of $333 million and adjusted net income of $78 million, per the earnings presentation.
Financial update
Coinbase's total revenue was stable from Q2 2026, and transaction revenue was $590 million, per the earnings presentation. Net income was $719 million.
Adjusted EBITDA reached $333 million, up 60% Q/Q, marking Coinbase's 15th consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA. Coinbase described the drivers this way: "$1.2B total revenue was flat Q/Q against a backdrop of a decline in Total Market Crypto Trading Volume (-10% Q/Q) and flat Average Crypto Market Capitalization," and "Transaction revenue declined 1% Q/Q as Crypto Asset Volatility reached multi-year lows."
Diversification
49% of net revenue came from Subscription and Services revenue in Q3 2026, which was $570 million, per the earnings presentation. That was within Coinbase's Q3 outlook of $500 million to $580 million, and up from a 41% share of net revenue in Q3 2025.
The lines inside Subscription and Services revenue were stablecoin revenue of $307 million (up 5% Q/Q), blockchain rewards of $86 million (up 3%), interest and finance fee income of $69 million (up 4%) and other Subscription and Services revenue of $109 million (down 4%). Coinbase describes this part of the business as providing "diversification and support independent of transaction revenue."
Coinbase One paid subscribers
Paid Coinbase One subscribers grew 24% Y/Y to an all-time high in Q3 2026, per the earnings presentation.
Coinbase One is Coinbase's paid subscription product. Paid Coinbase One Subscribers have 3.5x higher average revenue per user, 4.2x higher balances per user and 50%+ higher long-term trading retention than non-subscribers.
Prediction markets update
Prediction markets surpassed $200 million in annualized revenue (ARR) in Q3 2026, and daily traders (DAU) grew more than 60% Q/Q, per the release.
Prediction markets revenue has seen 82% quarterly compound growth since launch, and Coinbase points to a diversified "contract mix with non-sports categories showing strong growth through seasonally slower sports months." In the release, Brian Armstrong, Co-Founder and CEO, said: "Prediction markets have been one of the fastest-growing products in Coinbase history, growing even through slower sports months driven by crypto contracts where we have a strong right to win."
